cards.a: An Ethernet WAN service carried across a metro/service provider network, offering cost, speed, and simple L2/L3 models with service types such as E-LINE, E-LAN, and E-TREE, delivered via EoMPLS/pseudowire or VPLS/EVPN.

cards.q: Why choose Metro Ethernet as a WAN?
cards.a: Because Ethernet is ubiquitous (familiar skills), fast (1/10/100 G), cheaper than TDM, and scales via EVPN.

cards.q: What are the three EVC service types and their connectivity models?
cards.a: E-LINE is point-to-point (site links), E-LAN is multipoint any-to-any, and E-TREE is hub-spoke (root/leaf).

cards.q: Which delivery technologies are used for point-to-point versus multipoint Metro Ethernet?
cards.a: EoMPLS (L2VPN pseudowire) is used for point-to-point, while VPLS/EVPN provide multipoint L2VPN delivery.

cards.q: What is the role of QinQ (802.1ad) in Metro Ethernet?
cards.a: QinQ stacks VLANs: customer tags (C-tags) ride inside service tags (S-tags) at the provider edge to deliver carrier Ethernet.

cards.q: What is the key difference between Metro Ethernet and MPLS L3VPN for routing?
cards.a: L2 Metro Ethernet keeps routing with the customer, while L3 MPLS L3VPN hands routing to the provider; control is EVPN/VPLS versus MP-BGP respectively.

cards.q: What is EVPN in connection with Metro Ethernet?
cards.a: EVPN is a modern BGP + VXLAN-based L2/L3 service that scales beyond VPLS.

cards.q: Which commands verify Metro Ethernet pseudowires and EVPN services?
cards.a: show l2vpn forwarding and show l2vpn service for pseudowires; show ethernet service, show evpn evi, and show bridge-domain for EVPN/bridge checks.

cards.q: A point-to-point Metro Ethernet link is down. What is the likely cause and check?
cards.a: A failed pseudowire is likely; check show l2vpn forwarding.

cards.q: Multipoint Metro Ethernet connectivity is broken. What is the likely cause and check?
cards.a: A VPLS/EVPN problem is likely; check show evpn evi and MP-BGP state.

cards.q: Metro Ethernet traffic is tagged incorrectly. What is the likely cause and check?
cards.a: A QinQ tag mismatch is likely; check the ethernet service tag configuration.

cards.q: How are E-LINE, E-LAN, and E-TREE defined in one line?
cards.a: E-LINE is point-to-point, E-LAN is any-to-any, and E-TREE is hub-spoke.
